checks.name: right_reasons
checks.detail: Cannot be checked: explanations are in terms of embedding dimensions, which have no meaning of their own.

strengths.text: SHAP and LIME are faithful: removing the inputs flagged as important really does move the score.

weaknesses.text: Barely better than guessing: test AUC 0.591 (0.5 is a coin flip).
Explanations are about 32 embedding dimensions with no meaning of their own. A probe shows they partly encode degree (R² 0.36) and ring membership (AUC 0.81).
LIME gives a different answer when re-run on the same account (rank agreement between runs: LIME 0.68).

checklist.text: Test on data collected after your training data. Behaviour drifts, and a validation split from the same period hides that.
Choose the decision threshold on held-out data for the precision you need; a wrongly banned real user costs more than a missed bot.
Keep a fixed audit sample of labelled accounts and re-run the explanations on it after every retrain.
List which inputs an attacker can change cheaply (posting rate, hashtags, timing) and test the model with those changed.
Do not deploy as a detector. At this accuracy it flags real users about as often as fakes.
checklist.because: Barely better than guessing: test AUC 0.591 (0.5 is a coin flip).

checklist.text: If you must explain decisions to users or moderators, prefer a model with interpretable inputs.
